item.title: Settlers smash foundations of Palestinian family's homes in West Bank
item.description: Militant Israeli settlers smashed the foundations of two homes belonging to a Palestinian family in the West Bank on Thursday, after settler attacks prevented the family from returning to them in ...
item.content:encoded:
Settlers smash foundations of Palestinian family's homes in West Bank Reuters | Updated: 26-11-2026 23:58 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 23:58 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Militant Israeli settlers smashed the foundations of two homes belonging to a Palestinian family in the West Bank on Thursday, after settler attacks prevented the family from returning to them in defiance of an Israeli court order. Security cameras showed the settlers bringing a bulldozer to the hilltop two-storey houses on either side of a road in the village of Jaloud at around 1 a.m. and spending about an hour damaging the houses. The family said it had been forced out months ago. In a visit to the area, Reuters reporters saw that the concrete foundations of the homes had been partially broken. "This latest escalation is a direct consequence of the lack of law enforcement and the sense of impunity enjoyed by the perpetrators," said Ghiath Nasser, a lawyer representing the owners of the houses in court. The demolition follows a surge of settler violence in which settlers have encroached on Palestinian villages, with an average of 53 settler attacks per week since the start of 2026, according to UN figures. The Israeli military issued a statement condemning Thursday's attack as “a serious criminal act” and said it was investigating the incident. What appeared to be Israeli security forces were visible visiting the area around the homes. In most cases, such incidents do not result in prosecution. According to Israeli rights group Yesh Din, 93.6% of investigations into settler violence cases are closed without indictments. “They want to demolish the houses so that we cannot return to them,” said Wael Tubasi, one of the owners of the homes. He said the deadline for the Israeli military to remove the settlers had passed, but Reuters reporters saw settlers in the area throughout the day. The Israeli military said a closed military zone order was in effect in the area and it was illegal for settlers to enter. It said settlers dispersed after the military arrived. Israel occupied the West Bank after a 1967 war, and has built hundreds of settlements there. UN bodies, Palestinians and most countries view the settlements as illegal under international conventions, a stance Israel disputes, and as an obstacle to peace. WATCHING THEIR HOMES FROM AFAR The Tubasi family now live in a small house in Jaloud, near the West Bank city of Nablus, with a direct view of the homes they were forced to flee. For months they have seen settlers move freely through their homes, while living in a small dwelling behind the two houses. “Even though there is a court order, and the army is required to remove them from the area entirely, not just return us to our homes, it's still not being implemented,” said Tubasi. In September, after the court order, the Israeli military escorted the family back to their houses. Ten minutes after they arrived, around 200 settlers attacked them, forcing the military and the family to retreat, family members said. The settlers then burned the houses and broke much of the furniture inside, they said, and since then they have been unable to return. “I'm forbidden from reaching my home, while the settlers have the right to remain inside. What rights are there?” said Aedah Tubasi, Wael’s mother. In April, settlers built a tent near the Tubasi family's homes. They began attacking the family, set fire to their homes, cut their water and electricity, and blocked roads to the houses, the family said. After three months, settlers appeared at their door and told them they had an hour to leave or be killed "like the Dawabsheh family," Aedah quoted them as saying. An 18-month-old child, his mother and father were killed when settlers set fire to the home of the Dawabsheh family in the West Bank village of Duma in 2015.

item.title: "Pull back all military aggression from Europe": Trump’s fresh appeal to Putin for Ukraine peace deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he wants Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back military aggression" across Europe, expressing hope that a peace agreement between Moscow and Kyiv ...
item.content:encoded:
"Pull back all military aggression from Europe": Trump’s fresh appeal to Putin for Ukraine peace deal US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he wants Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back military aggression" across Europe, expressing hope that a peace agreement between Moscow and Kyiv could be reached soon. ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 22:31 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 22:31 IST

US President Donald Trump with Russian President Vladimir Putin. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Thursday said he wants Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back military aggression" across Europe, expressing hope that a peace agreement between Moscow and Kyiv could be reached soon. Writing on Truth Social, Trump stated that he had discussed the Russia-Ukraine war extensively during his recent conversation with Putin in China, noting that he hoped those discussions would result in an agreement between the two nations. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly," Trump wrote. Pointing to the ongoing loss of life in the conflict, Trump added that he viewed an agreement as a strong possibility. "I really believe this is a strong possibility. Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH, and will be a Great Tribute to everyone!" he said. Trump's remarks followed a day after his meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida. According to a joint statement issued after their meeting, Trump and Rutte stated that the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in Iran were among the primary subjects of their discussions. The joint statement noted that both leaders discussed the necessity for Russia to refrain from moves that could deliberately or inadvertently widen the war, alongside the urgency of securing a peaceful settlement as swiftly as possible. "Lastly, we discussed the importance of continuing to expand defence spending and investment in our industrial base, both in the United States and across NATO," the statement read. Trump further said he briefed Rutte on his recent discussions with Putin. "It was an honour meeting with Secretary General of NATO, Mark Rutte, last night at Mar-a-Lago, where many topics were discussed, and in which I updated him on my talks with President Putin," he wrote. Trump's latest statements follow an unprecedented meeting involving three major world leaders, Trump, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, on November 19 in Shenzhen, China. The three leaders met at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, marking their first-ever trilateral meeting. Their discussions spanned international security, the Russia-Ukraine war and nuclear arms control, with Trump calling the gathering historic and stating that the three nations bore a collective responsibility to uphold global peace. Following the meeting, the three nations released a joint peace declaration, though it stopped short of announcing any concrete agreement on arms reduction. (ANI)

item.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial over 2018 alleged rape of actress, court rules
item.description: As per the publication, the 77-year-old actor could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. However, he has denied the allegations and maintained that their encounters were consensual.
item.content:encoded:
French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial over 2018 alleged rape of actress, court rules As per the publication, the 77-year-old actor could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. However, he has denied the allegations and maintained that their encounters were consensual. ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 21:53 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 21:53 IST

French actor Gerard Depardieu (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial in connection with a rape allegation made by a young actress in 2018, as per The New York Times. The decision was taken by a Paris appeals court on Thursday, nearly eight years after the woman first filed a complaint against the actor. As per the publication, the 77-year-old actor could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. However, he has denied the allegations and maintained that their encounters were consensual. The case was filed by Charlotte Arnould, who was 22 at the time. She had visited Depardieu’s Paris home twice in August 2018, seeking his help in entering the film industry. She later accused the actor of raping her during both visits, The New York Times said. While the police initially dropped the case in 2019 due to a lack of evidence, prosecutors reopened the investigation in 2020 after Arnould took legal steps to have it resumed. The appeals court has ordered Depardieu to stand trial over the alleged rape during the first visit. However, it did not include the allegation relating to the second visit in its decision, according to the publication. As per the publication, speaking outside the courtroom, Arnould’s lawyer Carine Durrieu Diebolt called the decision a victory for her client and said, “It is a victory for her, given that Gerard Depardieu is going to stand trial for rape. We are eagerly awaiting this trial.” Depardieu’s lawyers, meanwhile, called the decision a partial win as the court did not order a trial over the second allegation. The actor can still challenge the decision before France’s highest court, the Court of Cassation. According to The New York Times, in an open letter published in Le Figaro in October 2023, Depardieu denied forcing Arnould and said that their encounters were consensual. Recalling the two visits, he wrote, “A woman came to my house a first time, light-footed, going up to my room of her own free will. Today she says she was raped there. She came back a second time. There was never any coercion, violence or protest between us.” The actor has faced allegations of sexual abuse from more than 20 women in recent years, making him a central figure in France’s debate over sexual misconduct in the film industry, as per The New York Times. As per the publication, in a separate case, Depardieu was convicted last year of sexually assaulting two women who worked with him on the sets of the 2021 film ‘Les Volets Verts’. The victims, a set decorator and an assistant director, had accused him of sexual assault. He received an 18-month suspended prison sentence and was added to France’s national register of sex and violent offenders. Although he initially appealed the conviction, he withdrew his appeal last week. Depardieu has appeared in more than 230 films and received several awards during his career. Despite the allegations, he has also received public support from prominent figures in France, including President Emmanuel Macron, who had defended the actor in 2023, according to The New York Times. (ANI)

item.title: Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos set to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president: Report
item.description: Former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to be nominated by European Union (EU) leaders as the next President of the European Central Bank (ECB), succeeding Christine Lagarde, after ...
item.content:encoded:
Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos set to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president: Report Former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to be nominated by European Union (EU) leaders as the next President of the European Central Bank (ECB), succeeding Christine Lagarde, after the Netherlands decided to back his candidacy, Reuters reported on Thursday. ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 21:20 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 21:20 IST

Former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to be nominated by European Union (EU) leaders as the next President of the European Central Bank (ECB), succeeding Christine Lagarde, after the Netherlands decided to back his candidacy, Reuters reported on Thursday. The development comes nearly a month after Lagarde announced her decision to step down as ECB President before the completion of her eight-year term. De Cos currently serves as the General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), a position he assumed on July 1, 2025. The BIS promotes international monetary and financial cooperation and serves as a bank for central banks. According to his official profile on the BIS website, De Cos served as Governor of the Bank of Spain from 2018 to June 2024. During this period, he was also a member of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank, its principal monetary policy decision-making body. He also chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, which develops global regulatory standards for banks, giving him experience in both monetary policy and international banking regulation. Earlier, in a statement issued on November 6, the Eurogroup President confirmed that two candidates had been nominated for the position of ECB President - Pablo Hernandez de Cos from Spain and Klaas Knot from the Netherlands. The process to appoint a new ECB President was initiated following Lagarde's announcement in October. In an official statement issued on October 29, the ECB said that Lagarde would "step down from her position on 7 February 2027." Lagarde has been serving as the President of the European Central Bank since November 2019. Her original term was scheduled to conclude in October 2027. Under the EU's appointment procedure, the European Council appoints the ECB President following a recommendation by the Council of the European Union and consultations with the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council. The ECB President is appointed for a non-renewable term of eight years. The European Central Bank is responsible for maintaining price stability in the euro area, primarily through monetary policy decisions. Its interest rate decisions are closely monitored by global financial markets. (ANI)
